title: Steam Fish with Hollandaise Sauce
description: Delicately steamed white fish fillets served with a silky classic Hollandaise sauce and buttered seasonal vegetables for an elegant Continental main course.

items: 2 fresh white fish fillets (sea bass, cod, or snapper, 160–180 g each)
Freshly ground white pepper, to taste
125 g unsalted butter, melted and clarified
A pinch of cayenne pepper or white pepper
Baby carrots, blanched and sautéed in butter

instructions: Season the fish fillets lightly with sea salt and white pepper.
Brush each fillet with olive oil and place on parchment paper or banana leaf. Top with a lemon slice and a sprig of dill or tarragon.
Steam at 85–90°C (185–195°F) for 6–8 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
To prepare the Hollandaise, whisk the egg yolks and white wine vinegar in a heatproof bowl over a bain-marie until pale and thickened.
Gradually whisk in the warm clarified butter until fully emulsified and silky.
Season the sauce with salt, lemon juice, and cayenne or white pepper. Keep warm without overheating.
Arrange the steamed fish on warm serving plates.
Spoon the Hollandaise sauce over the fish.
Serve with steamed asparagus or French beans and buttered baby carrots.
Finish with microgreens, chervil, and a drizzle of lemon zest oil if desired.
chefTips: Steam the fish gently to preserve its delicate texture and moisture.
Keep the Hollandaise around 60°C (140°F) to prevent splitting.
If the sauce becomes too thick, whisk in a teaspoon of warm water.
Serve immediately on warm plates for the best presentation and flavor.
